facts.text: Central Florence is entirely walkable and a car is a liability, not an asset - much of the historic center is a restricted traffic zone (ZTL) with automatic fines for unauthorized vehicles.
The Uffizi Gallery and Accademia (David) both benefit enormously from advance timed-entry booking - walk-up lines in peak season can run multiple hours.

Restaurants with a tout standing outside physically inviting you in, especially near the Duomo or Ponte Vecchio, are reliably lower quality and higher price than places a few streets into Santo Spirito or Sant'Ambrogio.

A "bistecca alla fiorentina" (Florentine steak) is traditionally priced and served by weight (often per 100g/hg) - always confirm the total expected price before ordering, as this has been a documented source of bill-shock for tourists.
Tuscan cuisine is meat-forward (bistecca, wild boar, cured meats); vegetarian options are more available in modern trattorias than traditional ones.
Many museums and churches close on Mondays; check specific opening days before building an itinerary around a single museum-heavy day.
